introduction_markdown: Duration: two and a half hours. This paper is arranged in two sections, A and B. Answer ALL questions in Sections A and B. Section A: answer ALL 15 questions in the spaces provided; the mark allocation for each question is indicated. Section B: answer ALL four questions; all questions in Section B carry equal marks (15 marks each). You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the sets $A = \{0 \le x < 4,\ x \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ and $B = \{-1 \le x < 2,\ x \in \mathbb{Z}\}$, list the elements of the set $A$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
$x$ is an integer with $0 \le x < 4$, so $x$ can be $0, 1, 2, 3$ (the value $4$ is excluded).

**Answer: $A = \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the sets $A = \{0 \le x < 4,\ x \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ and $B = \{-1 \le x < 2,\ x \in \mathbb{Z}\}$, list the elements of the set $B$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
$x$ is an integer with $-1 \le x < 2$, so $x$ can be $-1, 0, 1$ (the value $2$ is excluded).

**Answer: $B = \{-1, 0, 1\}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the sets $A = \{0 \le x < 4,\ x \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ and $B = \{-1 \le x < 2,\ x \in \mathbb{Z}\}$, draw a Venn diagram to represent the sets.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Elements common to both sets: $A \cap B = \{0, 1\}$. Elements only in $A$: $\{2, 3\}$. Elements only in $B$: $\{-1\}$.

**Diagram to draw:** a rectangle for the universal set $\xi = \{-1, 0, 1, 2, 3\}$ (the union $A \cup B$), with two **overlapping** circles labelled $A$ and $B$.

- In the overlap (intersection) write $0$ and $1$.
- In the part of circle $A$ outside the overlap write $2$ and $3$.
- In the part of circle $B$ outside the overlap write $-1$.

All five elements appear exactly once and none lies outside the circles.
